thereto: in addition to that; also, besides this
whence: from which place, source, or origin
thereby: by means of that; as a result of it
hereby: by this means; through this act or statement
aught: anything at all, any whatever thing
nought: nothing; zero, having no value or existence
twain: two; a pair of things or persons
betimes: early; in good time; at times
thereof: of that thing or matter just mentioned
thou: you, used to address one person (archaic)
thyself: yourself, used when addressing one person
shalt: shall; you will or must (archaic verb form)
shouldst: should; you ought to (archaic verb form)
canst: can; are able to (archaic verb form)
knoweth: knows; is aware of (archaic verb form)
doeth: does; performs or carries out (archaic verb form)
seeth: sees; perceives or looks upon (archaic verb form)
sayeth: says; speaks or declares (archaic verb form)
wotteth: knows; is aware of (archaic verb form)
drinketh: drinks; takes liquid in (archaic verb form)
bindeth: binds; ties or restrains (archaic verb form)
wrought: worked, made, or brought about by effort
cleave: to cling closely; or to split apart
penance: self-punishment or austerity undertaken to atone for sin
sloth: laziness; reluctance to act or exert effort
votary: a devoted follower, worshipper, or believer
rites: ceremonies performed according to religious custom
sages: wise and learned people, especially spiritual teachers
scrolls: rolled sheets of writing, such as sacred texts
hallowed: made holy; greatly honoured and revered
steeds: horses, especially fine or spirited ones (poetic)
charioteer: the driver of a horse-drawn chariot in battle
conch: a large sea shell blown as a horn or trumpet
tempest: a violent storm with strong winds
rewardment: a reward or recompense given for deeds
largesse: generous gifts given freely to others
soothfast: true and faithful; steadfast in truth
enjoined: commanded or ordered by authority or duty
equanimity: calm, even-tempered composure under any circumstance
equability: evenness of temper; steady calmness of mind
untaught: not instructed; lacking formal teaching or learning
nirvana: the state of spiritual liberation and end of rebirth
prakriti: primal matter or nature, the material source of creation
atman: the individual self or soul, the eternal inner being
rishi: a sage or seer who received sacred Hindu hymns
brahman: a member of the priestly class; or the universal spirit
sudra: a member of the lowest of the traditional Hindu social classes
rakshasa: a demon or evil spirit in Hindu legend
suras: the gods or celestial beings in Hindu belief
adityas: a group of ancient Hindu solar deities
maruts: storm gods associated with winds in Hindu belief
sankhya: one of the six classical Hindu philosophical systems
vedantist: a follower of the Vedanta, a Hindu philosophy of the Upanishads
aswattha: the sacred fig tree, a symbol of the eternal world
shlokas: verses of Sanskrit poetry, each typically of two lines
karmabandha: the bondage or binding effect of action and its results
sense-storms: violent surges of the senses that disturb the mind
sense-life: a life governed mainly by pleasure of the senses
unmoved: not disturbed or shaken by emotion or outside events
lusts: strong, uncontrolled desires for pleasure or possession
unwilling: not inclined or ready to do something
heedless: careless; not paying attention to consequences
ignorance: lack of knowledge, understanding, or awareness
enlightened: spiritually awakened; having true knowledge and wisdom
dread: deep fear or anxiety about something terrible
fixity: a state of being firmly fixed or unchanging
